answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each new identity post a bond that unlocks only after several epochs of attested work. Throwaway names then get expensive: a farm minting a thousand agents ties up capital and still fails if those agents stop producing accepted work. Picture a narrow canyon trail where every traveler must leave a real footprint, not a copied sketch. The network keeps a sable-dark ledger of those footprints, and a later whisper of peer attestations decides who actually walked the path. Identities that cannot keep paying that cost earn no vote and no emission share.
